dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Well, that's this problem solved. Next, we need to consider the next event... Should we increase the number of ways in which people can draw prizes...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Other than the festival, we can't afford to dilly-dally on any of our plans...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Ah, speaking of which, the books from "that place" in Ritou will probably arrive soon. I can use them as reference...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Should I do a special issue... Hmm, a serial release would be fine, too...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Ah, speaking of which, the books from "that place" in Ritou will probably arrive soon. I can use them as reference...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Oh, me? I work at Yae Publishing House. I'm in charge of the planning and promotion of all our projects.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Take the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest, for example. It was I who proposed, organized, and set it up.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: My boss Hiratsuka didn't approve of that originally. Not sure if it was because he was too much of a stick in the mud or just didn't want to do more work...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Thankfully, I pushed harder and promised that I would complete all of the work myself. Only then did the contest become a thing in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: I mean, just look! Hasn't "This Novel Is Amazing!" become our most important project now? Every light novel reader pays rapt attention to the result of the contest — all thanks to me!

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Actually, I have been planning for some new project recently. Just you wait and see.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The books from what place in Ritou now?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Eh? You heard that? Well... Never mind. You're an outlander right? You should be able to understand me.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Because of the Sakoku Decree, it's getting harder and harder to get foreign books. But my job relies on creativity, so I have to learn new stuff, right?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Therefore, I will secretly ask people who can enter and leave Inazuma to bring some new books from outside. If there are some confiscated books from Ritou, I will also tell them to smuggle them in.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: You have to keep this a secret for me. In exchange, I'll let you read the new books.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, that's how we'll do it... Oh, alright, goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could I ask about a novelist by the name of Sumida...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Sumida... Huh, speaking of that, I haven't actually seen her in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: She bade me a solemn farewell sometime back, saying that she was on her way out to travel, and that I should await her grand victory in the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Even though, you know, she hasn't actually finished a single novel ever...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not a single one?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Nope. Her logic jumps all over the place, and my standards are pretty strict, so her projects often wind up abandoned half-baked.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Still, I have rather high hopes for her. The stories written by such people tend to be the best.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: I hope she can keep her promise, either way, and send a manuscript worthy of the grand prize to me as a souvenir of her travels.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The books from what place in Ritou now?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Well, I mean, my job relies on creativity, so I have to learn new stuff, right?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: That's why I often ask friends to send me new books from overseas. If there are some impounded books over in Ritou, I will also tell them to bring them in.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: You have to keep that whole "impounded books" business a secret for me, alright? In exchange, I'll let you read the new stuff next time.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Ugh, how am I supposed to contact these two authors in this situation...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Contact who now?

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Oh! Traveler, it's you... Thank goodness you're here. I was just in need of someone's help!

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Here's the problem: Yae Publishing House's annual novel-writing competition is about to begin, and as is our rule, we plan to invite a few of our writers to serve on the judging panel.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: However, we have two writers who are neither Inazuman, nor do they currently reside in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: As you know, the present circumstances prevent us from inviting outlanders here.

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: But if we fail to inform the writers of such an important matter, that would also be inappropriate...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: So I thought that if someone could at least send them a gift, the basic courtesies would at least be satisfied. And we could also attach a letter discussing future manuscripts— *cough* I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Aratani
dialogues.text: Would you be willing to help me out?

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: We're counting on you, Traveler.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Chang the Ninth's story, known as the "First Apprentice of Guhua," is a tale about the first apprentice of a famed martial arts school in Liyue and a young girl from Inazuma whom he took on as a junior apprentice.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: If you were to ask me, the themes and plot are just a little outdated by this point, but enough readers buy it to keep sales up.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: We often ask people to send some letters to him to suggest certain changes he might make in future works to perhaps make a breakthrough...

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: But we have never received a reply. Perhaps the letters were lost on the way, or...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Who's Zhenyu?

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Now this one, I have no idea about. It's likely a pen name of some sort.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: But the book "A Legend of Sword"? That one's an earth-shatterer and a world-shaker, make no mistake!

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Both the setting and the story have sent veritable shocks throughout the literary world!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, where do I find this writer, then...

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: Hmm. I believe that this writer also lives in Liyue. According to a traveling merchant who brought this book back to Inazuma, he first found this text at Wanwen Bookhouse.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: I think that if you ask the staff at Wanwen Bookhouse, you should be able to find this author.

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: However... *cough* Well, never mind that for now. Here are the presents and the letters. I'm putting this in your reliable hands, Traveler!

response.speaker: Aratani
response.text: One of them is named Zhenyu, and the other is... Chang the Ninth.
